grand_strategy.reading:
The UAE under Mohamed bin Zayed runs the grand strategy of a small, rich state that has chosen to buy depth rather than inherit it: money turns into ports, ports into
clients, clients into reach, and reach into a seat at every table. The 'little Sparta' reading fits the 2015-2025 years, when Abu Dhabi built a ring of bases, terminals and proxies from
Mukalla to Berbera to Benghazi and held down the Islamist wing of the Arab world. Luttwak's reversal came in two beats. First, the December 2025 - January 2026 collapse of the Yemeni
bridgehead under Saudi pressure and Somalia's cancellation of every deal showed that a network of clients is strong against the weak and fragile against a neighbour that can fly its
own aircraft. Second, the war that began on 28 February 2026 hit the other half of the model, the hub: the state that sold itself as the safest place in the Gulf took the largest share of Iranian fire,
lost more than 90% of its Jebel Ali traffic and found that its only real shield was the United States, tied to it by a commitment and no treaty. The response is a double move - a harder
line (secret strikes, Iron Dome from Israel, the OPEC exit, the Netanyahu visit of 27 September) and a wider hedge (China, India, France, a Syria in which Abu Dhabi now invests).
The Saudi question is the pivot: the July-September 2026 thaw (the Mansour visit) looks like a truce in a rivalry that continues on the Horn, Sudan and Yemen, not a settlement; the Houthi
attacks on Saudi airports in October 2026, which the UAE condemned in the strongest terms, give both a common enemy again. One signal that is not a row: the UAE did not sign the Arab-Islamic statement against Israel's
recognition of Somaliland (December 2025). The dataset still lists UAE membership of OPEC; it ended on 1 May 2026.

stances.note: Stable de facto alignment, not a treaty: the US Air Force has flown from Al Dhafra since 2002, Trump's Abu Dhabi stop of 15 May 2025 produced the AI framework and the USD 1.4tn pledge, the UAE took the largest share of Iranian fire in the 2026 war on the US-Israeli side, and Washington answered by easing chip and arms exports (July 2026) and promising a 'commitment' to UAE security (Rubio, 24 Jun 2026). Graded ally on the ONTOLOGY rule (stable de facto alignment); the missing treaty is written into the card as a constraint, and the same Rubio statement is the only formal assurance. Not partner, because the UAE fought alongside and hosts US forces; not reluctant_ally, because no source shows Abu Dhabi resisting the alignment (the friction is about being left exposed, not about the tie). Bond none: interest.
